_readme: Single source of truth for every business fact on the site. status: confirmed | unconfirmed | not-offered. Anything unconfirmed renders as a marked placeholder and blocks `npm run build:launch`. TEDDY_CONFIRMATIONS.md is generated from this file by `npm run punchlist`.

businessName.label: Business name
businessName.source: Samson (verbal). Public identity search 2026-10-16 found no matching truck/trailer shop.
businessName.ask: Exact legal and trading name, and how it is written on the shop sign and paperwork.

tradeLine.label: Trade
tradeLine.ask: Confirm the trade, and whether to say heavy-duty, diesel, fleet or owner-operator.

location.label: City
location.ask: Shop city, or whether the business is mobile only.

serviceScope.label: Service scope
serviceScope.value: Diagnostics, repair and inspections for tractors, straight trucks and trailers.
serviceScope.source: Generic description of the proposed trade. Not provided by the business.
serviceScope.ask: Which equipment the shop works on, and anything it does not work on.

serviceModel.label: Where the work happens
serviceModel.ask: Shop only, mobile, roadside calls, or a mix? Any drop-off or towing arrangements?

serviceArea.label: Service area
serviceArea.ask: Cities, highways or radius covered. Is Fort Worth in?

hours.label: Hours
hours.ask: Opening hours by day, and holiday closures.

emergency.label: Emergency and after-hours calls
emergency.ask: Is there 24/7 or after-hours service? If so, what exactly, and is there a separate number?

estimates.label: Estimate and approval process
estimates.ask: How are estimates given and approved? Any diagnostic fee? (Do not publish prices unless Teddy asks to.)

phone.label: Phone number
phone.ask: Main phone, and whether it takes texts.

address.label: Street address
address.ask: Street address, and parking or yard access for trucks with trailers.

licensing.label: Licenses and certifications
licensing.ask: Any certifications, dealer authorizations or inspector credentials, with documents.

insurance.label: Insurance
insurance.ask: Whether to mention insurance at all, and exact wording approved by Teddy.

warranty.label: Warranty on repairs
warranty.ask: Any written warranty on parts or labor, and its exact terms.

reviews.label: Customer reviews
reviews.ask: Real reviews with permission to quote, or a link to the Google Business Profile.

formDestination.label: Where repair requests go
formDestination.source: No intake process approved. The request form is a non-submitting preview.
formDestination.ask: Who receives requests (email, text, CRM), how fast they reply, and privacy handling for customer details.

domain.label: Domain and hosting
domain.ask: Existing domain, who controls DNS, and who approves going live.

services.name: Brakes & air systems
services.summary: Brake inspection, adjustment and component replacement, plus air-system leak and compressor diagnosis.

services.name: DOT annual inspections
services.summary: Periodic inspections of commercial vehicles against the minimum standards in 49 CFR Part 396, Appendix A.
services.source: Generic category. Rule: 49 CFR 396.17 and Appendix A to Part 396 (eCFR).

services.name: Engine & aftertreatment diagnostics
services.summary: Fault-code diagnosis and repair for diesel engines, including DPF, DEF and EGR-related issues.

services.name: Electrical & lighting
services.summary: Tractor and trailer lighting, wiring, connectors and ABS sensor faults.

services.name: Suspension, axles & landing gear
services.summary: Springs, air bags, bushings, axle components and trailer landing gear.

services.name: Tires & wheel ends
services.summary: Tire repair and replacement, wheel-end inspection and bearing service.

services.name: Trailer body & doors
services.summary: Roll-up and swing doors, hinges, floors and structural repairs on dry vans and flatbeds.

services.name: Reefer unit service
services.summary: Troubleshooting for refrigerated trailer units. Brand authorization would need to be confirmed.
services.source: Generic category. Often a specialist or dealer job, so it may not apply.

services.name: Preventive maintenance
services.summary: Scheduled service intervals: fluids, filters and inspections.

faq.q: What should I have ready when I call?
faq.a: Your unit number and type (tractor, straight truck, dry van, reefer, flatbed), where the unit is right now, what it is doing (warning lights, noises, leaks, won't start), whether it is loaded, and any deadline such as an inspection due date.
faq.source: General guidance written for this concept. Makes no claim about the business.

faq.q: What does a DOT periodic inspection cover?
faq.a: Federal rules require commercial motor vehicles to be inspected at least once every 12 months. The inspection must cover, at a minimum, the components listed in Appendix A to 49 CFR Part 396, such as brakes, steering, lighting, tires and coupling devices.

faq.q: Do you work on trailers as well as tractors?
Do you come to me, or do I bring the unit in?
How do estimates and approvals work?
Do you take emergency or after-hours calls?
